page: Microsoft Azure L96s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a maximum clock frequency of 4.2 GHz. The compute configuration delivers 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography accelerators like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Memory capacity is configured at 768 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation that aligns with high-density data workloads. The primary hardware highlight of the L96s_v4 is its bundled local storage array, offering 23,040 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity. Synthetic memory testing demonstrates strong performance characteristics, recording 6,198.6 GB/sec for small-block cached reads and 222.04 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, alongside a write throughput of 94.04 GB/sec.

Benchmark results highlight top-tier compute and throughput metrics across multiple suites. In Geekbench, the instance achieves a single-core score of 2,156 and a top-tier multi-core score of 21,790. PassMark testing records a multi-threaded CPU score of 85,426.93, with strong extended instructions (102,417.52) and encryption scores (84,140.49). Workload-specific benchmarks reflect these hardware capabilities: PassMark database operations reach 31,419.75, Redis SET throughput exceeds 102.15 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput hits 113.25 GB/sec. On CPU-driven large language model inference tests, prompt processing achieves 3,593.66 tokens/sec on 135M models and 35.80 tokens/sec on 70B models, while 70B text generation registers 4.18 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L96s_v4 provides high density by coupling massive local NVMe disk space with heavy compute capacity and large memory on a single virtual host. However, the local NVMe storage is ephemeral, requiring application-level data redundancy or replication strategies. The server is well suited for high-throughput NoSQL databases such as Cassandra and MongoDB, distributed relational databases, large-scale search indexing, in-memory caching layers with persistence, and real-time big data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L96s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Designed for disk-intensive and memory-heavy workloads, the system incorporates 768 GB of system memory and 23,040 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-decile multi-core compute capability, scoring 21,790 in Geekbench multi-core and 85,426.93 in PassMark CPU tests. Memory and storage subsystems deliver high throughput, achieving over 102 million Redis SET operations per second and 113.25 GB/sec in static web serving. Instruction set support includes AVX-512, AMX, and accelerated cryptography. Because the NVMe storage is local and non-persistent across deallocations, the instance is targeted at distributed data architectures, high-performance database clusters, big data analytics engines, and large caching nodes requiring rapid I/O.
